Drop unused levels of the factor group columns (dplyr backend method)

Source: R/group-by.R
group_trim.tbl_gpu.Rd

Native: dplyr::group_trim() on a grouped tbl_gpu finds the codes still used by each factor group column on the GPU (a distinct over that one column; only the at most n_levels + 1 distinct codes reach R), keeps the used levels in their original order (an ordered factor stays ordered), remaps the codes with gpu_remap_codes() and regroups with ungroup() + group_by(.drop = ), which also drops any fixed_keys left by .preserve = TRUE. Pending ops are computed first (the new level set depends on the data). An ungrouped table is returned unchanged, without looking at .drop, like dplyr. Shapes outside the allowlist (duplicated names, a factor group column without known levels) use the CPU fallback.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
group_trim(.tbl, .drop = dplyr::group_by_drop_default(.tbl))

Arguments

.tbl

A tbl_gpu object.

.drop

Whether the regroup drops empty groups.

Value

A tbl_gpu.
